mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Describe, from the electrical architect perspective, a CNES PASO concurrent-engineering/MBSE workflow for needs analysis, power budgets, power subsystem pre-sizing, technology trade-offs, and energy-balance simulations during nanosatellite preliminary phases. The pain points are mission/system complexity, highly agile observation planning, interlocked subsystem trade-offs, and tedious solar-panel/battery sizing.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Boundary covers satellite/mission common technical reference, orbital scenario/attitude over time, power budget by subsystem/mode, energy flows, and power subsystem model with solar generator, battery, regulators, bus topology, losses, temperature and end-of-life effects. It remains preliminary: manufacturer involvement, later lifecycle phases, formal requirements/V&V, and physical integration/testing are outside the demonstrated boundary.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: The workflow needs mission observation plan, orbital scenario/attitude, sun/earth angles, subsystem power consumption by mode, and EPS technology parameters. Limited behavioral knowledge is handled by reducing the global observation plan to a representative worst-case 48-hour scenario and by converting budgets/modes/ephemeris into executable power profiles and energy flows.
generality_reuse_mechanism: specific-mission model with reusable method only

key_evidence_quotes.quote: setting up a common technical reference (satellite description and mission), with the aim of producing system-level budgets

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper demonstrates a mission-specific 16U nanosatellite electrical-architecture model, not a mission-agnostic reference architecture. Reuse is mainly in the repeatable workflow, guidance steps, standardized file/input-output interfaces, and automated conversions between mission/system tools and Opalis. Do not add high-level abstraction or low-dynamics labels: the model includes detailed EPS simulation parameters and does not claim reuse because of behavioral minimalism.

evidence.quote: In the end, the most common process would then be the following:

It takes the CCSDS-like standard files generated by Simu-CIC (orbital scenario description) as an input in order to automatically convert the ephemeris data (such as sun angles) into flows for the solar generator.
The main added value of this process is that it allows to define an adaptable and interoperable model.
The presented use case describes the process for preliminary phases... but it could also be implemented for phases A/B/C/D... as long as the files standard is still respected.

toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.toolchain_architecture_and_data_flow: IDM-CIC defines the satellite/system/subsystem description and basic geometry and stores power-budget data. Simu-CIC defines the mission scenario and generates ephemeris. IDM-Power allocates IDM-CIC power-budget consumptions to modes and outputs a temporal power profile. Flows Manager converts Simu-CIC CCSDS-like ephemeris data into energy flows. Opalis combines the EPS architecture model, power profile and energy flows to run energy-balance simulations. IDM-View/IDM-Plot can visualize aspects of the system.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity: Continuity is claimed through a common database and standard/CCSDS-like file formats. Semantic continuity is demonstrated for power-budget-to-mode-to-profile and ephemeris-to-energy-flow transformations, but exact schemas and model semantics are not reported.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.software_hardware_system_integration_rea: Supports preliminary electrical architecture choices and component sizing; no direct hardware/software integration, flat-sat, manufacturing, or test readiness is demonstrated.
toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.availability_reproducibility: Tools and data flow are named, but model files, scenario files, scripts, precise schemas, and public repositories are not reported. Opalis is described as proprietary but open and CNES-developed.

eps_verification_specific.eps_requirements_represented_and_links: Formal requirements are not represented. Design criteria and acceptance thresholds are represented operationally through power budgets with margins, mission modes, end-of-life/temperature assumptions, nominal SOC cycling target of 75% to near 100%, and survival-case SOC minimum of 20%. These are linked to Opalis simulations via generated power profiles and energy-flow inputs.

verification_validation_artifacts.rationale: Worst-case observation and no-illumination survival scenarios, SOC acceptance thresholds, and simulation outputs are used as pre-physical feasibility checks.

pre_physical_development_verification_me.rationale: Mission/ephemeris, power loads and EPS architecture are virtually integrated and checked through repeated simulations and parameter variations before physical development.

eps_verification_specific.evidence_verification_artifacts_integrat: Simulation inputs are generated from system/mission model tools and imported into Opalis rather than being documented separately; however no formal requirements/V&V matrix is shown.

integration_test_readiness.rationale: No explicit links to hardware integration, software integration, flat-sat/testbed, environmental test, or operational validation are reported.

evidence_quotes.quote: Flight dynamics experts from CNES thus extracted from the global observation plan provided by the LESIA the worst case scenarios in terms of sun illumination, reducing it to a period of 48h only that could be used to size the power subsystem and still be representative of the whole mission.

In that case, a satisfactory equilibrium for the aforementioned power subsystem would thus be defined as a battery cycling between 75% and a bit less than 100% of state of charge, meaning that the energy production is sufficient to power the satellite as well as charging the battery during low illumination time windows, while still ensuring a sufficient margin in the eventuality of a satellite malfunction.

ivv_integration_level.rationale: The highest evidenced pre-physical IVV integration is simulation-in-the-loop: power profiles and ephemeris-derived energy flows are imported/generated through tool connections and used in Opalis simulations to check energy balance and SOC margins. The paper does not show trace-linked verification artifacts, a verification matrix, model-contained test procedures, SIL/HIL, or physical integration/test evidence.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text: The concurrent-engineering toolchain produces an adaptable and interoperable model in which mission or satellite-configuration changes can be studied quickly/easily.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.other_mechanism: Standardized CNES/CCSDS-like files exchanged between mission/system-description tools and Opalis power simulation.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: IDM-CIC system description, Simu-CIC ephemeris, IDM-Power profile, Flows Manager conversion, Opalis energy-balance model.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.other_metric_or_value_indicator: Qualitative instant/easy change-analysis claim; no measured time or effort.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: Authors state mission changes can be studied almost instantly and solar-panel configuration changes can be compared easily, but no timing or effort metric is reported.

evidence_source.quote: The main added value of this process is that it allows to define an adaptable and interoperable model. For instance, any change on the mission can be studied almost instantly by regenerating the corresponding ephemeris data.

additional_evidence.quote: Another example would be that any change on the configuration or structure of the satellite (for instance amount and position of the solar panel wings) can also be compared easily.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.threats_or_alternative_explanations: Ease and speed are asserted without a baseline or measured iteration times; improvements could depend on CNES tool familiarity and data-preparation effort.

claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.claim_text: The simulation workflow enables EPS sizing and stable energy-budget assessment under worst-case mission and environmental conditions.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.artifact_process_linked: Opalis power-subsystem model, energy flows from Simu-CIC/Flows Manager, power profile from IDM-Power, SOC thresholds and final architecture selections.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.other_metric_or_value_indicator: State of charge, energy balance, cell/accumulator series-parallel sizing, end-of-life assumptions.
claimed_outcomes_value_mechanisms_eviden.observed_effect_size_or_qualitative_effe: The reported stable configuration has SOC minimum 85% for nominal energy balance and survival scenario SOC minimum 27.7% against a 20% acceptable minimum.

evidence_source.quote: One last thing to mention is that the minimum SOC (State Of Charge) reached during the simulation is 85%

additional_evidence.quote: SOC initial = 80%, SOC min reached = 27.7%, and SOC min acceptable = 20%.

key_findings_by_rq.rq1: Provides a concrete, tool-mediated workflow for modeling mission scenario, satellite/system description, power budgets, and EPS architecture for a 16U nanosatellite, but not a general reusable MBSE reference model or minimal-behavior method.
key_findings_by_rq.rq2: Strongly relevant to integrability/interoperability and decision-support claims: common database, standardized files and plugins support parallel expert analyses, trade studies and electrical sizing. Evidence is mainly a single simulated use case.
key_findings_by_rq.rq3: Offers pre-physical simulation-based feasibility checks for EPS sizing and SOC acceptance thresholds, but lacks formal verification procedures, requirements traceability, test artifacts, or IVV model integration.
